note: Track steps-to-leaps, step 4: Do up to Sol by step over a drone, then two Easy Sol-stage tunes at 40 bpm, one starting on Sol, one learned in the named stages down to a cappella. Key and tempo are moves in place of the old Key selector (the second tune sits a step above the others and keeps that distance).

exercise.title: Five notes: Do up to Sol
exercise.why: Sol blends with the drone almost as well as Do, so it is a second place to check your pitch, and the steps down from it lead straight home.

cells.text:
Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows as a line on the staff. Sol is the ringed note. Sing from the low {{1}} up to {{5}} one step at a time, then step back down. Sing them on the note names.
Hold {{5}} for a moment at the top, and listen for it settling against the drone.
_Don't reach for high notes: start from the low {{1}}, so {{5}} stays easy._

This tune starts on Sol and steps down to Do. Tap its first note below to hear it. Then press Play below to hear the tune at {{=bpm}}: the mic starts with it. Sing along on the note names.
Practice until you can start on Sol without tapping it first.
{{?key}}In another key the notes are new, and the tune still steps down from Sol to Do.

Press Play below to hear the tune: the mic starts with it. This tune starts on Mi, steps up to Sol and comes home by step, a little lower in each bar. Sing along on the note names.
Sing along with the tune a few times. Then press Tune below to mute the tune, and sing it over the chords alone.
Once the names come without thinking, press Chords to mute the chords too, and sing the tune a cappella.
